Getting started
What you need to do this week

Follow these steps in order. Do not wait for the facilitation letter to start on the others.

1

Gather all your documents

Start collecting everything on the checklist below — bank statements, enrollment proof, residence permit, insurance, and photos. Do not wait for the facilitation letter to get started on the rest.

2

Fill in the VIDEX visa application form

Complete the official German short-stay visa form online. You will need your passport, travel dates, accommodation address in Germany, and purpose of visit.

Open VIDEX form
3

Book your embassy appointment in Skopje

Visit the German Embassy Skopje visa page to book your appointment slot. Slots fill up fast — do this as soon as possible, ideally before June 5th.

Embassy Skopje — book appointment
4

Wait for your visa facilitation letter

The facilitation letter is being arranged by the council and is expected very soon. Once you receive it, you will have everything needed to submit your full application.

5

Submit your application at the embassy

Attend your booked appointment with all documents. The German embassy typically takes around 20 working days to process Schengen visa applications, so timing is critical.

Frequently asked questions
Common questions answered

Everything you need to know about the German Schengen visa process.

The German embassy typically takes around 20 working days to process Schengen visa applications. This is why it is critical to book your appointment and submit all documents as early as possible — do not wait until the last minute.
No. The German embassy does not accept statements from digital/fintech banks such as Wise, Revolut, or Payoneer. You must provide a statement from a traditional bank account showing the past 3–6 months of transactions.
You need to provide a confirmed accommodation address in Germany — this can be a hotel booking confirmation, a hostel reservation, or a letter from relatives/friends hosting you. The address must be for the entire duration of your stay.
Yes, this is important. Your residence permit must have at least 2–3 months of validity remaining after your expected return date from Germany. If your permit is expiring soon, please address this urgently before applying for the visa.
Start by gathering all documents on the checklist. Volunteers from the facilitation team are available to help you fill in the VIDEX application form. Reach out via your Jamat group and someone will guide you through the process step by step.
Yes, travel health insurance is mandatory for a Schengen visa. It must cover the full duration of your stay and provide a minimum of €30,000 coverage for medical emergencies. Make sure the policy explicitly states it is valid for the Schengen area.
The visa facilitation letter is an official letter from the organising council confirming your participation in the Deedar program. It is currently being arranged and is expected very soon. Do not wait for this letter to start collecting your other documents — have everything else ready so you can move quickly once it arrives.
